# 🏢 opencode Pixel Office **Watch your opencode orchestrator and its subagents work live – in a top-down pixel-art office.** An opencode plugin that starts a tiny web server inside the opencode process and turns every session, tool call and delegation into office life: the boss hands out assignments on paper, the team works at their desks, and whoever has nothing to do takes a break in the lounge. ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.1.0-ffd43b) ![opencode](https://img.shields.io/badge/opencode-1.x%20%7C%202.x-ffd43b) ![oh-my-opencode](https://img.shields.io/badge/oh--my--opencode-slim%20%26%20classic-7048e8) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-node%20%E2%89%A5%2022.18-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white) ![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-40c057) ![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)
--- ## Contents - [Features](#-features) - [Screenshots](#-screenshots) - [Quick start](#-quick-start) - [Installation](#-installation) - [Configuration](#-configuration) - [Using the UI](#-using-the-ui) - [The office](#-the-office) - [Approvals & security](#-approvals--security) - [How it works](#-how-it-works) - [Troubleshooting](#-troubleshooting) - [Limitations](#-limitations) - [Development](#-development) - [Changelog](#-changelog) - [Licenses](#-licenses) ## ✨ Features | | | |---|---| | 👥 **A permanent team with names** | Otto (boss), Ella & Emil (explorers), Lotte (librarian), Orla (oracle), Fritz & Frieda (fixers), Dani (designer), Rita (reviewer) – each with their own desk. When a team is busy, a temp walks in and works on a laptop. | | 📄 **Paperwork** | Pick up the assignment from the boss's outbox → work on it at the desk (every file edit adds a page to the stack) → bring the report back to the inbox. | | 💬 **Live speech bubbles** | The current tool with a pixel icon (read, edit, bash, grep, web, task …), streamed text and reasoning. Monitors show code, a terminal or a browser. | | ☕ **Breaks** | Off-duty staff grab a coffee, watch TV, chill on a beanbag, play arcade games or ping-pong, check their phone, browse the web or pet the office cat. | | ✋ **Approvals in the UI** | Answer permission requests with *Allow once / Always allow / Reject* and stop running agents. | | 🔎 **Needs attention** | One queue across all rooms: approvals and questions, unresolved failures and agents with no activity for 10 minutes. | | 🧵 **Threads & timeline** | Who delegated to whom, plus working / waiting / retrying / idle / failed intervals with work and wait totals. | | 🏢 **Building** | One floor per project folder, one office per session, an elevator in between. | | 🌙 **Day & night** | Follows your local time; at night lit by monitors, lamps and a crystal ball. | | 📱 **Anywhere** | Desktop and phone, local or across your LAN/Tailscale (with a token). | | 📦 **One file** | A single self-contained `pixel-office.js` with zero runtime dependencies – no assets, CDNs or external calls. | ## 📸 Screenshots
At night with the timeline and a pending approval in Needs attention · below: the building with one floor per project Phone view
## ⚡ Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/gingerthighs/opencode-pixel-office.git cd opencode-pixel-office ./install.sh # Windows: .\install.ps1 ``` Start opencode, run a task, open **http://127.0.0.1:4777/**. Just want to look around first? `npm install && npm run mock` plays a demo scenario without opencode. ## 🚀 Installation ### Requirements | | | |---|---| | **opencode** | 1.x or 2.x. Works with plain opencode; shines with [oh-my-opencode](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-opencode) or oh-my-opencode-slim, which spawn subagents. | | **Node.js ≥ 22.18** | Only to **build** the plugin (it runs TypeScript directly). At runtime the plugin uses opencode's own runtime. | | **Browser** | Any current desktop or mobile browser. | ### Install script
🍎 macOS · 🐧 Linux · WSL ```bash ./install.sh ```
🪟 Windows (PowerShell) ```powershell .\install.ps1 ``` If the execution policy blocks the script: ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1 ```
The script installs the build dependencies, builds `dist/pixel-office.js` and copies it to `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\plugins\`). opencode 2.x picks it up while running; with 1.x restart opencode once. | Option | Effect | |---|---| | `--host 0.0.0.0` | make it reachable on your LAN / via Tailscale | | `--token auto` | require a token (generated and printed) – always use it together with `0.0.0.0` | | `--port 4800` | use a different port (default `4777`) | | `--project ` | install for one project only (`/.opencode/plugins`) | | `--skip-build` | use the existing `dist/pixel-office.js` | | `--uninstall [--purge]` | remove the plugin (`--purge` also deletes `pixel-office.json`) | Options for host, port and token are saved to `pixel-office.json` and kept on later runs. Example for a server on your home network: ```bash ./install.sh --host 0.0.0.0 --token auto ``` ### Update ```bash git pull ./install.sh # Windows: .\install.ps1 ``` opencode 2.x hot-reloads the new file; open browser tabs reconnect on their own. ### Uninstall ```bash ./install.sh --uninstall --purge ```
Manual installation (no Node.js needed with the release file) Download `pixel-office.js` from the [latest release](https://github.com/gingerthighs/opencode-pixel-office/releases/latest) and copy it to `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`. Settings go into `~/.config/opencode/pixel-office.json` (see [Configuration](#-configuration)). Or build it yourself: ```bash npm ci && npm run build cp dist/pixel-office.js ~/.config/opencode/plugins/pixel-office.js ```
## 🔧 Configuration Settings are read in this order (first one wins): 1. Environment variables of the opencode process 2. Plugin options, when the plugin is listed in `opencode.json`: `"plugin": [["", { "port": 4777 }]]` 3. `~/.config/opencode/pixel-office.json` – written by the installer 4. Defaults | Setting | Env variable | Default | | |---|---|---|---| | `port` | `PIXEL_OFFICE_PORT` | `4777` | | | `host` | `PIXEL_OFFICE_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | `0.0.0.0` for LAN / Tailscale | | `token` | `PIXEL_OFFICE_TOKEN` | – | open the URL once with `?token=…`, the browser keeps it in a cookie | | `allowedHosts` | `PIXEL_OFFICE_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | `[]` | host names allowed without a token (e.g. `box.tail1234.ts.net`); `localhost` and IP addresses always work. Env: comma-separated | | `debug` | `PIXEL_OFFICE_DEBUG` | `false` | write event samples to `pixel-office-events.jsonl` for diagnosis (see [Troubleshooting](#-troubleshooting)) | ```json { "port": 4777, "host": "0.0.0.0", "token": "your-secret-token" } ``` > [!TIP] > opencode 2.x starts a **background service** (`opencode serve --service`) that loads the plugins. Environment > variables you set after it started never reach it – that is what `pixel-office.json` is for. ## 🖱 Using the UI | Control | What it does | |---|---| | **Room tabs** | One tab per session (main session + its subagents). Rooms idle for more than two hours are hidden. | | **Needs attention** | Queue across all rooms. Click an entry to jump to the room and open the details. | | **▤ Building** | Overview with one floor per project folder; click an office to ride the elevator there. | | **Threads** | Lines from the boss to everyone working on one of their assignments. | | **Timeline** | Activity per agent below the office, with 15-, 60- or 120-minute windows. | | **Follow** | Stay on the current room while it's busy, then jump to the most recently active busy room. | | **All** | Also show rooms that went quiet. | | **Panel** | Click a person, desk or row for the activity feed, todos, edited files, tokens and controls. | URL parameters for links or a second screen: `?time=day|night`, `?threads=1`, `?timeline=1`, `?follow=0`, `?view=building`. ### Needs attention Ordered by urgency – approvals and questions first, then unresolved failures, then busy agents with no observed activity for 10 minutes – and oldest first within each group. "No activity" only means no events arrived; it does not prove an agent is stuck. New activity clears an entry, a new run clears a failure. While the browser is disconnected a warning is shown and the inactivity check pauses. On phones the queue starts collapsed. ### Timeline and history The timeline shows what the server **observed**: history starts when a session is first seen, earlier work is not guessed. Finished agents leave the office after 60 seconds but stay in the timeline; click their row for read-only details. History is kept **in memory only** – up to two hours, 1,000 finished sessions and 10,000 intervals, oldest first out (the UI marks truncated history). Reloading the page keeps it; restarting opencode or reloading the plugin clears it; deleting a session removes its record. Nothing is written to disk. ## 🗺 The office ``` ┌──────────┬────────┬────────┬──────────────────┐ │ BOSS │ ORACLE │ REVIEW │ LIBRARY │ │ Otto │ Orla │ Rita │ Ella·Emil·Lotte │ ├──────────┴────────┴────────┴──────────────────┤ │ HALLWAY │ ├───────────┬─────────────┬──┬──────────────────┤ │ STUDIO │ WORKSHOP │ │ TEMPS │ │ Dani │ Fritz·Frieda│ │ (laptops) │ ├───────────┼─────────────┤ ├──────────────────┤ │ CAT │ GAME │ │ LOUNGE │ │ CORNER │ ROOM │ │ TV·sofa·kitchen │ └───────────┴─────────────┴──┴──────────────────┘ entrance ``` | Agent (opencode / oh-my-opencode) | Team | Room | |---|---|---| | `orchestrator`, `sisyphus`, `atlas`, `hephaestus`, `prometheus`, `build`, `plan` | Boss | Boss office | | `explorer`, `explore`, `general` | Explorer | Library | | `librarian` | Librarian | Library | | `oracle`, `metis`, `momus`, `council` | Oracle | Oracle room | | `fixer`, `sisyphus-junior` | Fixer | Workshop | | `designer`, `frontend-ui-ux-engineer`, `multimodal-looker`, `document-writer` | Designer | Studio | | `reviewer`, `observer` | Reviewer | Review | | anything else, or when the team is busy | Temp | Temps room | Otto always takes the main session of a room. Subagents go to the matching free team member. ## 🔐 Approvals & security > [!IMPORTANT] > The UI shows prompts, file names and commands. By default it only listens on **`127.0.0.1`**. If you bind to > `0.0.0.0`, always set a `token` (or only expose it through Tailscale/a VPN). - **DNS-rebinding protection:** without a token the server only answers requests for `localhost`, IP addresses and names in `allowedHosts`. A malicious page that points its own domain at `127.0.0.1` gets `421`. - **Controls** (approvals, stop) go through `POST /api/control` and need: - a per-process nonce from the same-origin capabilities endpoint (refreshed after reconnects), - without a token: a loopback bind and a `localhost` Host header, - over the network: the token. - **Event forwarding** (`POST /api/ingest`, between opencode processes) needs a custom header that browsers can't send cross-site, because the CORS preflight is never approved. - **Forwarded controls** go back to the process that owns the session through a private loopback listener with a random per-process token. Its credentials never appear in UI snapshots. - **Token file:** the installer writes `pixel-office.json` with mode `600` (readable by you only). - **No third parties:** the font is embedded and the page loads nothing from other servers (strict CSP). - **Debug sampling** is off by default (see [Troubleshooting](#-troubleshooting)). Found a security issue? Please report it privately via [GitHub security advisories](https://github.com/gingerthighs/opencode-pixel-office/security/advisories/new) instead of opening a public issue. ## 🧩 How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph opencode["opencode process"] E["Event bus
session · tool · text · usage"] --> P["pixel-office.js
store (reducer)"] T["Tool hooks
execute.before/after"] --> P P --> S["HTTP + SSE
:4777"] end S -- "snapshot + diff ops" --> B["Browser
canvas office + panel"] B -- "POST /api/control
(approve, stop)" --> S S -. "permission reply
session interrupt" .-> opencode ``` - **One file, zero dependencies:** `build.ts` bundles the UI, the font and the server with esbuild into `dist/pixel-office.js`. The server uses `node:http`, which works in Bun and Node. - **opencode 1.x and 2.x:** classic hooks (`server` → `event`) and the new `setup(ctx)` API; `src/v2.ts` translates v2 events (`session.execution.*`, `session.tool.*`, `session.text/reasoning.*`, `form.*` …). - **Subagents** are child sessions with a `parentID`; sessions revived via `task_revive` are looked up once with `ctx.session.get`. - **Several opencode processes:** the first one owns the port, the others forward their events via `POST /api/ingest`. Failed batches retry in order with bounded backoff (backlog of up to 5,000 events). Approvals and stop requests are routed back to the process that owns the session. - **Hot reload:** when the plugin file changes, the new version takes over from the old server. ## 🩺 Troubleshooting
The page doesn't load - Is opencode running? opencode unloads plugins when no instance has been active for a while – opening the CLI is enough. - Check the log: search `~/.local/share/opencode/log/` for `pixel-office` (e.g. "failed to load plugin" or "Port … is taken").
"Host not allowed" (421) You opened the UI through a host name without a token. Use `localhost`/the IP address, add the name to `allowedHosts`, or set a `token`.
"Token required" Open the URL once with `?token=`; the browser stores it in a cookie. The installer prints the full URL, and the token is in `~/.config/opencode/pixel-office.json`.
Approve / Stop buttons are missing Controls only work on a loopback bind opened via `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`, or with a token. The panel shows the reason ("Controls off: …"). Questions (pick an option) are always answered in the terminal.
Port already in use Another opencode process already owns the port – that's intended, events are forwarded there. For a different port: `./install.sh --port 4800`.
Settings don't apply Use `pixel-office.json` instead of environment variables (`./install.sh --host … --token …`). opencode's background service doesn't see variables set after it started.
Inspecting events With `PIXEL_OFFICE_DEBUG=1` (or `"debug": true` in `pixel-office.json`) the first samples of each event type are written to `~/.local/share/opencode/log/pixel-office-events.jsonl`. Texts are shortened but still contain snippets of prompts and commands – so this is off by default, the file is readable by you only and capped at 256 KB.
## 🚧 Limitations - **Questions** (an agent asking you to pick an option) are shown, but must be answered in the terminal – opencode's plugin API cannot send answers. - **History** lives in memory and is lost when opencode restarts or the plugin reloads. - **Early history:** sessions that ran before the plugin loaded show up, but their past activity is unknown. - **Not on npm yet** – use the install scripts or the file from the releases page. ## 🛠 Development ```bash npm install npm run mock # demo without opencode: http://127.0.0.1:4777 (MOCK_SPEED=1 for fast, PIXEL_OFFICE_PORT to change) npm test # builds first; reducer, adapters, forwarding, controls, activity, UI, server protection npm run typecheck npm run build # → dist/pixel-office.js ``` Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. Please run `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` before opening a PR.
Project layout ``` src/ plugin.ts plugin entry (default export { id, server, setup }), singleton, host adapters instance.ts session ownership, snapshots, forwarding retries, control routing store.ts pure reducer: opencode events → UI ops, activity history v2.ts opencode 2.x adapter: v2 events + tool hooks → v1 events server.ts node:http – /, /app.js, /api/state, /api/events (SSE), /api/ingest, /api/control, /api/caps config.ts env / options / pixel-office.json web/ office.ts floor plan, walls, furniture, lights, pathfinding characters.ts staff (assignment workflow, breaks) + the office cat scene.ts rendering, staffing, threads, building, overlays controls.ts capabilities, nonce, control requests activity.ts interval clipping, totals, attention ordering attention.ts attention queue and connection warning dom.ts stable panel/queue/timeline updates panel.ts · timeline.ts · sprites.ts · bubbles.ts · roles.ts · state.ts · main.ts fonts/ Pixelify Sans (OFL), inlined at build time scripts/ install.ts cross-platform installer (called by install.sh / install.ps1) mock.ts demo scenario test/ node:test suites (npm test) ```

## [0.1.0] – 2026-10-25

First public release.

### Added

- opencode plugin (1.x hooks and 2.x `setup(ctx)` API) that serves a web UI from the opencode process.
- Top-down pixel-art office with walled rooms, a permanent named team, temps on laptops, a lounge with TV,
  a game room and a cat corner.
- Paper workflow: assignments from the boss's outbox, pages stack up with every edit, reports go back to the inbox.
- Live speech bubbles with tool icons, streamed text and reasoning.
- Side panel with assignments, activity feed, todos, edited files, tokens and cost.
- Approvals (*Allow once / Always allow / Reject*) and a two-step stop from the UI, routed to the opencode
  process that owns the session.
- Needs-attention queue across all rooms: approvals, questions, failures and inactive agents.
- Threads, an activity timeline with 15/60/120-minute windows and in-memory history.
- Building view with one floor per project and an elevator; day/night lighting; phone layout.
- Multi-process support: additional opencode processes forward their events to the one that owns the port.
- Cross-platform installer (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`) with `pixel-office.json` settings.
- Security: localhost-only default, optional token, DNS-rebinding protection, nonce-protected controls,
  strict CSP, embedded font, opt-in debug sampling.
